correctness.rationale: For a partition with k blocks, exactly B_k-1 strict coarsenings determine k at round one. At fixed k=n-r+1, the round-two count of strict atomic refinements with one pair is sum_i C(s_i,2), uniquely maximized at C(r,2) by type (r,1^(n-r)) for r>=3; T_2 was detected by round one. At round three, the counts of strict T_r predecessors yield b_r=sum_i C(s_i,r) after correcting the known self-exclusion. Upper-triangular binomial inversion reconstructs the full block-size multiplicity vector, exactly the S_n/full-order-automorphism orbit. The proof handles n=1,2. Independent construction of full strict-order pairs and bidirectional 1-WL for all partition lattices n=1..7 matched exactly the type classes.
residual_risks: Requires all strict refinement pairs and separate in-/out-neighbour counts; neither Hasse graph nor arbitrary poset identification covered. Three is an upper bound, not proved optimal.

value.rationale: Uniform orbit reconstruction in just three local counting rounds, independent of Bell-number-sized lattice order, is a nontrivial structural algorithmic lemma for a canonical combinatorial poset. The explicit mechanisms (atomic extremum and binomial moment inversion) may be reused for other relational structures and distinguish the full strict-order language from the cover graph.
residual_risks: Not a graph-isomorphism procedure against arbitrary inputs and no proven optimality of three rounds.
